claim: For the asymmetric \(I_{3322}\) Bell test with Alice detected perfectly, Bob assigning every no-click event to outcome \(0\), and the two-qubit state \(|\psi_\theta\rangle=\cos\theta|00\rangle+\sin\theta|11\rangle\), there is an explicit analytic measurement family \(\alpha_1=0\), \(\alpha_2=2\sqrt{\theta}\), \(\alpha_3=\pi/2\), \(\beta_1=2\theta/3\), \(\beta_2=-2\theta/3\), \(\beta_3=-2\sqrt{\theta}\) whose Bob-efficiency threshold satisfies \(\eta_B^{\mathrm{th}}=3/7+(25/49)\theta+O(\theta^2)\), and hence tends exactly to \(3/7\) as \(\theta\to0^+\). More generally, within the natural six-parameter weak-entanglement scaling \(\alpha_1=u\theta\), \(\alpha_2=a\sqrt{\theta}\), \(\alpha_3=\pi/2+c\sqrt{\theta}\), \(\beta_1=b\theta\), \(\beta_2=d\theta\), \(\beta_3=f\sqrt{\theta}\), the leading Bell coefficient is at most \(4/3\) relative to the no-click loss, so every member with positive leading Bell coefficient has limiting threshold at least \(3/7\); equality holds exactly when \(u=0\), \(af=-4\), \(b=2/3\), and \(d=-2/3\), with \(c\) arbitrary. This is a constructive and scaling-class result only: it does not prove that \(3/7\) is the global optimum over all qubit strategies or all possible asymptotic scalings.
integrity: The infinite asymptotic statement is proved from exact two-qubit probability formulas, Taylor expansions with analytic remainders, and an algebraic completed-square identity. Finite numerical evaluations are used only as replay checks. Prior numerical evidence is not promoted to a global theorem.
scientific_limitations: The sharpness statement is restricted to the displayed six-parameter weak-entanglement scaling class. No global qubit lower bound, no arbitrary-scaling optimality, no finite-theta optimum, and no noisy-detector theorem is claimed.
title: An exact \(3/7\) weak-entanglement limit for an analytic asymmetric \(I_{3322}\) qubit strategy
